## Overview

This document follows the structure of [Lecture
12](https://skdeshpande91.github.io/stat441_fall2026/lectures/lecture12.html)
(Bradley-Terry models; `BradleyTerry2::BTm`) and [Lecture
13](https://skdeshpande91.github.io/stat441_fall2026/lectures/lecture13.html)
(home-court advantage and tournament simulation where *every* simulation
is saved so that simple, joint, and conditional probabilities can all be
estimated afterwards).

We fit **two** Bradley-Terry models to the 2025–26 NBA regular season.

**Model 1: team strengths + home court** (Lecture 13). Every team $j$
gets a fixed latent strength $\lambda_j$ (one team is the reference with
$\lambda = 0$), and a single home-court term $\lambda_0$:

$$\operatorname{logit} \mathbb{P}(H \text{ beats } A) = \lambda_0 \cdot \mathbb{1}\{\text{H at home}\} + \lambda_H - \lambda_A .$$

**Model 2: dynamic offense/defense + home court.** Instead of one fixed
number per team, a team's strength *going into each game* is built from
its offensive and defensive scores at that moment:

$$\lambda_j(t) = \beta_O \, O_j(t) + \beta_D \, D_j(t),
\qquad
\operatorname{logit} \mathbb{P}(H \text{ beats } A \text{ at time } t) = \lambda_0 \cdot \mathbb{1}\{\text{H at home}\} + \lambda_H(t) - \lambda_A(t).$$

This is the "strengths depend on covariates" extension of Bradley-Terry
mentioned in the project description (`BradleyTerry2` fits it directly,
because covariates are allowed to vary from row to row, just like
`at.home` does in Lecture 13).

- $O_j(t)$ = team $j$'s **offensive score** before game $t$: points
  scored per game *above the league average*.
- $D_j(t)$ = team $j$'s **defensive score** before game $t$: points
  allowed per game *below the league average* (so higher is better for
  both).
- Both are **exponentially weighted** averages of the team's earlier
  games (recent games count more) and are **shrunk toward 0** early in
  the year when a team has few games. They only use games *already
  played*, so there is no look-ahead leakage in the fit.

We then **simulate the whole season, the play-in, and the playoffs at
least 10,000 times under each model**, saving every team's outcome in
every simulation.

::: callout-note
## How "dynamic" works inside the simulation

In Model 2 the simulated season is played in chronological order. After
each simulated game, both teams' offensive and defensive scores are
updated from the *simulated* points, so hot and cold streaks feed into
later win probabilities, just as in the real data. Points have to come
from somewhere, so the simulation also uses a small points model
(details below). The win/loss result is still drawn from the
Bradley-Terry probability; the points are then drawn *consistent with
that winner*.
:::

## Settings

```{r settings}
N_SIMS             <- 100000     
SEED               <- 2026
CHUNK              <- 1000      # simulations processed at a time (memory)
PARAM_UNCERTAINTY  <- TRUE      # draw model parameters from their sampling distribution each sim
SEASON             <- 2026      # hoopR convention: 2026 = the 2025-26 season
FOCUS_TEAM         <- "New York Knicks"

# Model 2 ("dynamic" ratings)
HALF_LIFE          <- 20        # a game's weight halves after this many of the team's later games
PRIOR_GAMES        <- 8         # shrinkage: equivalent number of "average" games every team starts with
TEST_FRAC          <- 0.20      # last 20% of the season held out for the predictive comparison

GAMES_CSV          <- NULL      # optional CSV with columns: date, home, away, home_pts, away_pts, [neutral]
SIMS_FILE          <- "nba_sims_2026.rds"
```

```{r load-data}
fix_names <- function(x) recode(x, "Los Angeles Clippers" = "LA Clippers")

if (!is.null(GAMES_CSV)) {
  games <- readr::read_csv(GAMES_CSV, show_col_types = FALSE)
  if (!"neutral" %in% names(games)) games$neutral <- FALSE
  if (!"date"    %in% names(games)) games$date    <- seq_len(nrow(games))
  games$date <- as.Date(games$date)
} else {
  raw <- hoopR::load_nba_schedule(seasons = SEASON)
  if (!"neutral_site" %in% names(raw)) raw$neutral_site <- FALSE
  games <- raw |>
    filter(season_type == 2) |>                      # 2 = regular season
    # Rows ESPN tags as regular season that are NOT part of the 82-game schedule:
    #   * the NBA Cup Championship game and All-Star weekend games
    #   (Cup group play AND Cup quarterfinals/semifinals DO count toward the 82, so they stay.)
    filter(is.na(notes_headline) |
             !grepl("Cup Championship|All-Star", notes_headline, ignore.case = TRUE)) |>
    filter(is.na(type_abbreviation) | !type_abbreviation %in% c("CC", "ALLSTAR")) |>
    # Postponed games leave a 0-0 placeholder row at the original date; the real result
    # appears again as a separate "Makeup from ..." row, so drop the placeholders.
    filter(!is.na(home_score), !is.na(away_score)) |>
    filter(as.numeric(home_score) + as.numeric(away_score) > 0) |>
    arrange(game_date, game_id) |>
    transmute(date = as.Date(game_date),
              home = home_display_name, away = away_display_name,
              home_pts = as.numeric(home_score), away_pts = as.numeric(away_score),
              # neutral-site games (NBA Global Games); the lecture handles neutral sites the same way
              neutral = coalesce(as.logical(neutral_site), FALSE) |
                grepl("Berlin|London|Mexico|Paris", notes_headline))
}

games <- games |>
  mutate(home = fix_names(home), away = fix_names(away))

# Drop non-NBA-team games (e.g. All-Star exhibitions: "Team Stripes", "World", ...)
is_real <- games$home %in% teams$team & games$away %in% teams$team
if (any(!is_real)) {
  bad <- c(games$home[!is_real], games$away[!is_real])
  cat("Dropping", sum(!is_real), "non-team games:", paste(unique(bad[!bad %in% teams$team]), collapse = ", "), "\n")
}

games <- games[is_real, ] |>
  mutate(ord = row_number()) |>
  arrange(date, ord) |>                       # chronological order (stable within a date)
  left_join(teams |> select(team, home_id = id), by = c("home" = "team")) |>
  left_join(teams |> select(team, away_id = id), by = c("away" = "team")) |>
  mutate(home_win = as.integer(home_pts > away_pts),
         at_home  = if_else(neutral, 0L, 1L),   # 1 = home team at its own arena, 0 = neutral site
         game_no  = row_number())

# ---- sanity checks -----------------------------------------------------------
gp <- table(c(games$home_id, games$away_id))
if (nrow(games) != 1230 || any(gp != 82)) {
  warning("Expected 1,230 games and 82 per team, got ", nrow(games),
          " games (per team: ", min(gp), "-", max(gp), ").")
}
cat(nrow(games), "games loaded,", sum(games$neutral), "at neutral sites.\n")
```

```{r actual-standings}
actual <- bind_rows(
  games |> transmute(id = home_id, w = home_win),
  games |> transmute(id = away_id, w = 1L - home_win)
) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(actual_wins = sum(w), actual_losses = n() - sum(w), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(teams, by = "id") |>
  group_by(conf) |>
  mutate(actual_conf_rank = rank(-actual_wins, ties.method = "min")) |>   # wins only; no tiebreakers
  ungroup()
```

### Building the dynamic offensive and defensive scores

For each team, we keep a running (exponentially decayed) tally over its
games *in chronological order*. Before every game we record each team's
current $O_j(t)$ and $D_j(t)$, then update the tallies using that game's
points:

$$O_j(t) = \frac{\sum_k w_k \,(\text{pts for}_k - \bar{p})}{\sum_k w_k + c},
\qquad
D_j(t) = \frac{\sum_k w_k \,(\bar{p} - \text{pts against}_k)}{\sum_k w_k + c},
\qquad
w_k = 0.5^{\,(\text{games since } k)/\text{half-life}},$$

where $\bar{p}$ is the league-average points per team per game and $c$
is `PRIOR_GAMES`. (Pace is not removed: only final scores are in the
schedule feed. See the limitations at the end.)

```{r dynamic-ratings}
LEAGUE_MEAN <- mean(c(games$home_pts, games$away_pts))
rho         <- 0.5^(1 / HALF_LIFE)

dynamic_ratings <- function(gm) {
  n <- nrow(gm)
  S_off <- S_def <- W <- numeric(n_teams)
  pre <- matrix(0, n, 4, dimnames = list(NULL, c("off_h", "def_h", "off_a", "def_a")))
  for (k in seq_len(n)) {
    h <- gm$home_id[k]; a <- gm$away_id[k]
    # ratings BEFORE the game (only past games used)
    pre[k, ] <- c(S_off[h] / (W[h] + PRIOR_GAMES), S_def[h] / (W[h] + PRIOR_GAMES),
                  S_off[a] / (W[a] + PRIOR_GAMES), S_def[a] / (W[a] + PRIOR_GAMES))
    # then update both teams with this game
    S_off[h] <- rho * S_off[h] + (gm$home_pts[k] - LEAGUE_MEAN)
    S_def[h] <- rho * S_def[h] + (LEAGUE_MEAN - gm$away_pts[k])
    W[h]     <- rho * W[h] + 1
    S_off[a] <- rho * S_off[a] + (gm$away_pts[k] - LEAGUE_MEAN)
    S_def[a] <- rho * S_def[a] + (LEAGUE_MEAN - gm$home_pts[k])
    W[a]     <- rho * W[a] + 1
  }
  list(pre = tibble::as_tibble(pre),
       end = tibble(team_id = seq_len(n_teams),
                    off = S_off / (W + PRIOR_GAMES), def = S_def / (W + PRIOR_GAMES)))
}

dyn   <- dynamic_ratings(games)
games <- bind_cols(games, dyn$pre)
```

```{r dynamic-plot}
bind_rows(
  games |> transmute(team = home, game_no, Offense = off_h, Defense = def_h),
  games |> transmute(team = away, game_no, Offense = off_a, Defense = def_a)
) |>
  filter(team == FOCUS_TEAM) |>
  arrange(game_no) |>
  mutate(team_game = row_number()) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Offense, Defense), names_to = "Score", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(team_game, value, colour = Score)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Offense = "#F58426", Defense = "#006BB6")) +
  labs(title = paste(FOCUS_TEAM, "- dynamic offensive and defensive scores"),
       subtitle = "Points per game vs. league average, going INTO each game (higher = better)",
       x = "Team's game number", y = "Score (points/game vs. average)")
```

## Fitting the models

### Model 1: team strengths + home court (Lecture 13)

Games are grouped by (home team, away team, neutral-site flag);
`at.home` is 1 for home-arena games and 0 for neutral sites, exactly as
in Lecture 13.

```{r fit-bt1}
fit_bt1 <- function(gm) {
  res <- gm |>
    group_by(home, away, at_home) |>
    summarise(home.win = sum(home_win), away.win = sum(1 - home_win), .groups = "drop")
  df <- data.frame(home.win = res$home.win, away.win = res$away.win)
  df$home.team <- data.frame(team = factor(res$home, levels = teams$team), at.home = res$at_home)
  df$away.team <- data.frame(team = factor(res$away, levels = teams$team), at.home = 0)
  BradleyTerry2::BTm(
    outcome = cbind(home.win, away.win),
    player1 = home.team, player2 = away.team,
    formula = ~ team + at.home,
    refcat  = teams$team[1],
    id      = "team",
    data    = df)
}

fit1 <- fit_bt1(games)
lambda_hat  <- BradleyTerry2::BTabilities(fit1)
lambda0_hat <- unname(coef(fit1)["at.home"])

cat(sprintf("Model 1 home-court term: lambda0 = %.3f log-odds -> %.1f%% home win prob. between equal teams\n",
            lambda0_hat, 100 * plogis(lambda0_hat)))
```

### Model 2: dynamic offense/defense + home court

Now every *game* is its own row, because the covariates change from game
to game. Each team's data frame carries `at.home` and its pre-game
offensive and defensive scores (`off_rtg`, `def_rtg`). `BTm`
automatically uses the *difference* between the two teams' covariates.

```{r fit-bt2}
fit_bt2 <- function(gm) {
  df <- data.frame(home.win = gm$home_win, away.win = 1 - gm$home_win)
  df$home.team <- data.frame(team = factor(gm$home, levels = teams$team), at.home = gm$at_home,
                             off_rtg = gm$off_h, def_rtg = gm$def_h)
  df$away.team <- data.frame(team = factor(gm$away, levels = teams$team), at.home = 0,
                             off_rtg = gm$off_a, def_rtg = gm$def_a)
  # (BradleyTerry2 notes that ability is modelled by predictors with no team random effect; that is intended.)
  suppressWarnings(
    BradleyTerry2::BTm(
      outcome = cbind(home.win, away.win),
      player1 = home.team, player2 = away.team,
      formula = ~ off_rtg + def_rtg + at.home,
      id      = "team",
      data    = df))
}

fit2 <- fit_bt2(games)
kable(summary(fit2)$coefficients, digits = 4,
      caption = "Model 2 coefficients (log-odds per 1 point/game of offensive or defensive score)")
```

### Do dynamic offense/defense scores help? Predictive comparison

We compare both models, plus a "home court only" baseline, on log-loss
(lower is better), Brier score (lower is better), and accuracy.
"Out-of-sample" means the models are refit on the first
`r percent(1 - TEST_FRAC)` of the season and scored on the remaining
games.

```{r compare}
pred_bt1 <- function(fit, gm) {
  ab <- BradleyTerry2::BTabilities(fit)[, "ability"]
  plogis(ab[gm$home] - ab[gm$away] + coef(fit)["at.home"] * gm$at_home)
}
pred_bt2 <- function(fit, gm) {
  cf <- coef(fit)
  plogis(cf["off_rtg"] * (gm$off_h - gm$off_a) + cf["def_rtg"] * (gm$def_h - gm$def_a) +
           cf["at.home"] * gm$at_home)
}
metrics <- function(p, y) {
  p <- pmin(pmax(unname(p), 1e-9), 1 - 1e-9)
  c(`Log-loss` = -mean(y * log(p) + (1 - y) * log(1 - p)),
    Brier = mean((p - y)^2), Accuracy = mean((p > 0.5) == y))
}

n_train <- floor(nrow(games) * (1 - TEST_FRAC))
train <- games[seq_len(n_train), ]
test  <- games[-seq_len(n_train), ]

fit1_tr <- fit_bt1(train); fit2_tr <- fit_bt2(train)
base_p  <- mean(train$home_win)

bind_rows(
  tibble(Evaluation = "In-sample (all games)", Model = "Home court only",
         !!!as.list(metrics(rep(mean(games$home_win), nrow(games)), games$home_win))),
  tibble(Evaluation = "In-sample (all games)", Model = "Model 1 (team strengths)",
         !!!as.list(metrics(pred_bt1(fit1, games), games$home_win))),
  tibble(Evaluation = "In-sample (all games)", Model = "Model 2 (dynamic O/D)",
         !!!as.list(metrics(pred_bt2(fit2, games), games$home_win))),
  tibble(Evaluation = "Out-of-sample (last games)", Model = "Home court only",
         !!!as.list(metrics(rep(base_p, nrow(test)), test$home_win))),
  tibble(Evaluation = "Out-of-sample (last games)", Model = "Model 1 (team strengths)",
         !!!as.list(metrics(pred_bt1(fit1_tr, test), test$home_win))),
  tibble(Evaluation = "Out-of-sample (last games)", Model = "Model 2 (dynamic O/D)",
         !!!as.list(metrics(pred_bt2(fit2_tr, test), test$home_win)))
) |> kable(digits = 3)
```

Model 1 spends 30 parameters on team strengths; Model 2 uses only 3
(offense, defense, home court). The out-of-sample rows are the fairer
comparison.

```{r calibration-plot}
}
```

## Simulation engine

Everything is vectorised across simulations: each function takes a
vector of teams (one entry per simulation) and returns a vector of
winners. Both models share the **same** seeding, play-in, and playoff
code; they differ only in how regular-season games are simulated and in
the team strengths used for playoff games.

Common simplifications:

- **Tiebreakers:** regular-season ties are broken randomly (no
  head-to-head / division rules).
- **Play-in:** 7v8 winner is the 7 seed; the loser hosts the winner of
  9v10 for the 8 seed.
- **Series:** best-of-7, 2-2-1-1-1, higher seed has home court; the
  Finals give home court to the team with more regular-season wins.
- **Parameter uncertainty:** each simulation draws its own model
  parameters from a multivariate normal with the fitted coefficients and
  covariance matrix (`PARAM_UNCERTAINTY`).
- **Model 2 in the playoffs:** team strength is frozen at each team's
  *end-of-regular-season* offensive and defensive scores (their form
  going into the playoffs).

### Shared tools

```{r engine-common}
mvn_draw <- function(cf, V, n) {
  if (!PARAM_UNCERTAINTY) {
    B <- matrix(cf, length(cf), n)
  } else {
    L <- t(chol(V))
    B <- cf + L %*% matrix(rnorm(length(cf) * n), ncol = n)
  }
  rownames(B) <- names(cf)
  B
}

# --- one game: `home` and `away` are team-id vectors (length n); P = list(h, Theta) ---
play_game <- function(home, away, P) {
  n   <- length(home); idx <- seq_len(n)
  eta <- P$h + P$Theta[cbind(home, idx)] - P$Theta[cbind(away, idx)]
  ifelse(runif(n) < plogis(eta), home, away)
}

# --- best-of-7, team `a` has home court (games 1,2,5,7 at a) ---
play_series <- function(a, b, P) {
  n <- length(a); idx <- seq_len(n)
  d <- P$Theta[cbind(a, idx)] - P$Theta[cbind(b, idx)]
  a_home <- c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)
  wins_a <- 0
  # Playing all 7 games and checking for >= 4 wins gives the same winner distribution
  # as stopping once a team reaches 4.
  for (g in 1:7) wins_a <- wins_a + (runif(n) < plogis(d + if (a_home[g]) P$h else -P$h))
  ifelse(wins_a >= 4, a, b)
}

# --- series where home court goes to the lower "seed score" ---
series_by_seed <- function(t1, s1, t2, s2, P) {
  swap <- s2 < s1
  a <- ifelse(swap, t2, t1); b <- ifelse(swap, t1, t2)
  w <- play_series(a, b, P)
  t1_won <- w == t1
  list(win = w, win_seed = ifelse(t1_won, s1, s2), lose = ifelse(t1_won, t2, t1))
}

# --- one conference: play-in + 4 rounds. S: 15 x n matrix of team ids ordered by rank ---
sim_conference <- function(S, P, rounds_won, playoff_seed) {
  n <- ncol(S); idx <- seq_len(n)
  rec <- function(mat, team, value) { mat[cbind(team, idx)] <- value; mat }

  w78  <- play_game(S[7, ], S[8, ], P)
  l78  <- ifelse(w78 == S[7, ], S[8, ], S[7, ])
  w910 <- play_game(S[9, ], S[10, ], P)
  g3   <- play_game(l78, w910, P)
  T8   <- rbind(S[1:6, , drop = FALSE], w78, g3)          # row = playoff seed (1..8)
  for (s in 1:8) playoff_seed <- rec(playoff_seed, T8[s, ], s)

  sd <- function(s) rep(s, n)
  a <- series_by_seed(T8[1, ], sd(1), T8[8, ], sd(8), P)
  b <- series_by_seed(T8[4, ], sd(4), T8[5, ], sd(5), P)
  c <- series_by_seed(T8[3, ], sd(3), T8[6, ], sd(6), P)
  d <- series_by_seed(T8[2, ], sd(2), T8[7, ], sd(7), P)
  for (x in list(a, b, c, d)) rounds_won <- rec(rounds_won, x$lose, 0L)
  e <- series_by_seed(a$win, a$win_seed, b$win, b$win_seed, P)
  f <- series_by_seed(c$win, c$win_seed, d$win, d$win_seed, P)
  for (x in list(e, f)) rounds_won <- rec(rounds_won, x$lose, 1L)
  g <- series_by_seed(e$win, e$win_seed, f$win, f$win_seed, P)
  rounds_won <- rec(rounds_won, g$lose, 2L)

  list(champ = g$win, rounds_won = rounds_won, playoff_seed = playoff_seed)
}
```

### Model 1 regular season

```{r engine-bt1}
cf1 <- coef(fit1); V1 <- vcov(fit1)

regseason_bt1 <- function(n) {
  B <- mvn_draw(cf1, V1, n)
  P <- list(h = B["at.home", ],
            Theta = rbind(0, B[paste0("team", teams$team[-1]), , drop = FALSE]))   # 30 x n (ref team = 0)
  eta <- P$Theta[games$home_id, , drop = FALSE] - P$Theta[games$away_id, , drop = FALSE] +
         outer(games$at_home, P$h)
  list(home_win = matrix(runif(length(eta)) < plogis(eta), nrow = nrow(eta)), P = P)
}
```

### Model 2 regular season (dynamic)

To update offensive and defensive scores inside the simulation we need
simulated **points**. We fit a simple points model to the real games,

$$\text{pts}_{\text{team } i \text{ vs. opp } j} = \mu + \eta \cdot \mathbb{1}\{\text{home}\} + a_i + d_j + \varepsilon,
\qquad \varepsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2),$$

where $a_i$ is team $i$'s true offensive level and $d_j$ is how many
points opponent $j$ tends to allow. In the simulation, the game winner
is drawn from the Bradley-Terry probability computed from the teams'
*current simulated* scores. Then the final margin is drawn from the
points model **conditional on that winner** (a truncated normal), and
the total points from the points model, so that the points a team scores
and allows are consistent with the result. Those points update both
teams' scores before the next game.

```{r engine-bt2}
# ---- points model (used only to generate points in the Model 2 simulation) ----
pts_long <- bind_rows(
  games |> transmute(pts = home_pts, is_home = at_home,
                     off_team = factor(home, levels = teams$team), def_opp = factor(away, levels = teams$team)),
  games |> transmute(pts = away_pts, is_home = 0L,
                     off_team = factor(away, levels = teams$team), def_opp = factor(home, levels = teams$team))
)
fit_pts   <- lm(pts ~ is_home + off_team + def_opp, data = pts_long)
sigma_pts <- sigma(fit_pts)
cfp <- coef(fit_pts); Vp <- vcov(fit_pts)
cat(sprintf("Points model: residual sd = %.1f pts/team/game; home effect = %.2f pts\n",
            sigma_pts, cfp["is_home"]))

# ---- chronological batches: every team appears at most once per batch ----
# A game depends only on the earlier games of its two teams, so processing games in
# "levels" gives exactly the same results as processing them one at a time.
make_batches <- function(gm) {
  last <- integer(n_teams); b <- integer(nrow(gm))
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(gm))) {
    bk <- max(last[gm$home_id[k]], last[gm$away_id[k]]) + 1L
    b[k] <- bk; last[gm$home_id[k]] <- bk; last[gm$away_id[k]] <- bk
  }
  unname(split(seq_len(nrow(gm)), b))
}
batches <- make_batches(games)

cf2 <- coef(fit2); V2 <- vcov(fit2)
cs <- function(M, v) M * rep(v, each = nrow(M))        # multiply column j of M by v[j]

regseason_bt2 <- function(n) {
  B     <- mvn_draw(cf2, V2, n)
  b_off <- B["off_rtg", ]; b_def <- B["def_rtg", ]; b_home <- B["at.home", ]
  Q     <- mvn_draw(cfp, Vp, n)
  mu    <- Q["(Intercept)", ]; eta_p <- Q["is_home", ]
  Aef   <- rbind(0, Q[paste0("off_team", teams$team[-1]), , drop = FALSE])   # 30 x n
  Def   <- rbind(0, Q[paste0("def_opp",  teams$team[-1]), , drop = FALSE])   # 30 x n
  s     <- sqrt(2) * sigma_pts                  # sd of both the margin and the total

  S_off <- S_def <- W <- matrix(0, n_teams, n)
  home_win <- matrix(FALSE, nrow(games), n)

  for (ix in batches) {
    H <- games$home_id[ix]; A <- games$away_id[ix]; ah <- games$at_home[ix]; G <- length(ix)

    # pre-game dynamic scores for both teams (30 x n state -> G x n)
    offH <- S_off[H, , drop = FALSE] / (W[H, , drop = FALSE] + PRIOR_GAMES)
    offA <- S_off[A, , drop = FALSE] / (W[A, , drop = FALSE] + PRIOR_GAMES)
    defH <- S_def[H, , drop = FALSE] / (W[H, , drop = FALSE] + PRIOR_GAMES)
    defA <- S_def[A, , drop = FALSE] / (W[A, , drop = FALSE] + PRIOR_GAMES)

    # Bradley-Terry win probability for the home team
    eta <- cs(offH - offA, b_off) + cs(defH - defA, b_def) + outer(ah, b_home)
    hw  <- matrix(runif(G * n) < plogis(eta), nrow = G)
    home_win[ix, ] <- hw

    # points consistent with the winner (margin ~ truncated normal, total ~ normal)
    m_exp <- outer(ah, eta_p) + Aef[H, , drop = FALSE] + Def[A, , drop = FALSE] -
             Aef[A, , drop = FALSE] - Def[H, , drop = FALSE]
    t_exp <- matrix(rep(2 * mu, each = G), nrow = G) + outer(ah, eta_p) +
             Aef[H, , drop = FALSE] + Def[A, , drop = FALSE] + Aef[A, , drop = FALSE] + Def[H, , drop = FALSE]
    p_pos <- pnorm(m_exp / s)
    u     <- matrix(runif(G * n), nrow = G)
    q     <- ifelse(hw, (1 - p_pos) + u * p_pos, u * (1 - p_pos))
    q     <- pmin(pmax(q, 1e-10), 1 - 1e-10)
    Marg  <- m_exp + s * qnorm(q)
    Tot   <- t_exp + s * matrix(rnorm(G * n), nrow = G)
    hp    <- (Tot + Marg) / 2
    ap    <- (Tot - Marg) / 2

    # update both teams' running offense/defense tallies
    S_off[H, ] <- rho * S_off[H, , drop = FALSE] + (hp - LEAGUE_MEAN)
    S_def[H, ] <- rho * S_def[H, , drop = FALSE] + (LEAGUE_MEAN - ap)
    W[H, ]     <- rho * W[H, , drop = FALSE] + 1
    S_off[A, ] <- rho * S_off[A, , drop = FALSE] + (ap - LEAGUE_MEAN)
    S_def[A, ] <- rho * S_def[A, , drop = FALSE] + (LEAGUE_MEAN - hp)
    W[A, ]     <- rho * W[A, , drop = FALSE] + 1
  }

  # playoff strength = end-of-regular-season offensive/defensive scores
  off_end <- S_off / (W + PRIOR_GAMES); def_end <- S_def / (W + PRIOR_GAMES)
  list(home_win = home_win,
       P = list(h = b_home, Theta = cs(off_end, b_off) + cs(def_end, b_def)))
}
```

### One chunk of seasons + postseasons

```{r engine-chunk}
simulate_chunk <- function(n, model, sim_offset = 0L) {
  rs  <- if (model == "bt1") regseason_bt1(n) else regseason_bt2(n)
  P   <- rs$P
  idx <- seq_len(n)

  wins <- rowsum(rs$home_win + 0, games$home_id) + rowsum(1 - rs$home_win, games$away_id)  # 30 x n

  # seeding within each conference (random tiebreak)
  conf_rank <- matrix(NA_integer_, n_teams, n)
  S_list    <- vector("list", 2)
  for (cf in 1:2) {
    ids <- teams$id[teams$conf_id == cf]
    w   <- wins[ids, , drop = FALSE] + matrix(runif(length(ids) * n, 0, 0.5), nrow = length(ids))
    ord <- apply(w, 2, function(x) order(-x))
    S   <- matrix(ids[ord], nrow = length(ids))
    for (r in seq_len(nrow(S))) conf_rank[cbind(S[r, ], idx)] <- r
    S_list[[cf]] <- S
  }

  rounds_won   <- matrix(NA_integer_, n_teams, n)   # NA = missed playoffs
  playoff_seed <- matrix(NA_integer_, n_teams, n)
  east <- sim_conference(S_list[[1]], P, rounds_won, playoff_seed)
  west <- sim_conference(S_list[[2]], P, east$rounds_won, east$playoff_seed)
  rounds_won   <- west$rounds_won
  playoff_seed <- west$playoff_seed

  # NBA Finals: home court to the team with the better regular-season record
  e <- east$champ; w <- west$champ
  score_e <- -(wins[cbind(e, idx)] + runif(n, 0, 0.5))
  score_w <- -(wins[cbind(w, idx)] + runif(n, 0, 0.5))
  fin <- series_by_seed(e, score_e, w, score_w, P)
  rounds_won[cbind(fin$lose, idx)] <- 3L
  rounds_won[cbind(fin$win,  idx)] <- 4L

  tibble(
    model        = model,
    sim          = rep(idx + sim_offset, each = n_teams),
    team_id      = rep(seq_len(n_teams), times = n),
    wins         = as.vector(wins),
    conf_rank    = as.vector(conf_rank),
    playoff_seed = as.vector(playoff_seed),
    # -1 = missed playoffs / lost play-in, 0 = lost R1, 1 = lost R2, 2 = lost conf finals,
    #  3 = lost Finals, 4 = champion
    rounds_won   = coalesce(as.vector(rounds_won), -1L)
  )
}
```

## Run the simulations

Each simulation replication is a complete 1,230-game season, play-in,
and playoffs. As in Lecture 13, we save every team's results in every
simulation, so we can later estimate simple events, joint events, and
conditional probabilities from the same table.

```{r run-sims}
run_model <- function(model) {
  set.seed(SEED)
  starts <- seq(0L, N_SIMS - 1L, by = CHUNK)
  bind_rows(lapply(starts, function(s) simulate_chunk(min(CHUNK, N_SIMS - s), model, s)))
}

model_labels <- c(bt1 = "Model 1 (team strengths)", bt2 = "Model 2 (dynamic O/D)")

t0 <- Sys.time()
sims <- bind_rows(run_model("bt1"), run_model("bt2")) |>
  left_join(teams |> select(team_id = id, team, conf), by = "team_id") |>
  mutate(model = factor(model_labels[model], levels = model_labels))

# integrity checks: exactly one champion per sim, 8 playoff teams per conference per sim
stopifnot(
  all(sims |> group_by(model, sim) |> summarise(k = sum(rounds_won == 4), .groups = "drop") |> pull(k) == 1),
  all(sims |> filter(!is.na(playoff_seed)) |> count(model, sim, conf) |> pull(n) == 8)
)

saveRDS(sims, SIMS_FILE)
cat(sprintf("2 models x %s simulated seasons x 30 teams = %s rows in %.0f s. Saved to %s\n",
            comma(N_SIMS), comma(nrow(sims)),
            as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs")), SIMS_FILE))
```

`sims` has one row per **model × simulation × team**: `wins`,
`conf_rank` (1–15), `playoff_seed` (1–8 after the play-in; `NA` if
missed), and `rounds_won`.

```{r knicks-summary}
knicks_summary <- function(d) {
  c(round(mean(d$wins), 1),
    percent(mean(d$wins >= k_actual$actual_wins), 0.1),
    round(mean(d$conf_rank), 2),
    names(which.max(table(d$conf_rank))),
    percent(mean(d$conf_rank == 1), 0.1),
    percent(mean(d$conf_rank <= 2), 0.1),
    percent(mean(!is.na(d$playoff_seed)), 0.1),
    percent(mean(d$rounds_won >= 3), 0.1),
    percent(mean(d$rounds_won == 4), 0.2))
}
tab <- sapply(split(k_sims, k_sims$model), knicks_summary)
rownames(tab) <- c("Mean simulated wins",
                   paste0("P(simulated wins ≥ actual ", k_actual$actual_wins, ")"),
                   "Mean simulated East rank", "Most likely East rank",
                   "P(East #1 seed)", "P(East top 2)", "P(make playoffs)",
                   "P(win the East)", "P(win the title)")
kable(tab, caption = paste0("Actual: ", k_actual$actual_wins, " wins, East rank ", k_actual$actual_conf_rank,
                            " (by wins; no tiebreakers)"))
```

## Was the title an anomaly?

Championship probabilities for every team, under both models (Monte
Carlo standard errors are at most about 0.5 percentage points with
100,000 simulations):

```{r title-odds}
title_odds <- sims |>
  group_by(model, team, conf) |>
  summarise(mean_wins  = mean(wins),
            p_playoffs = mean(!is.na(playoff_seed)),
            p_finals   = mean(rounds_won >= 3),
            titles     = sum(rounds_won == 4),
            p_title    = titles / N_SIMS,
            se         = sqrt(p_title * (1 - p_title) / N_SIMS),
            .groups = "drop")

title_odds |>
  select(model, team, mean_wins, p_title) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = c(mean_wins, p_title), names_vary = "slowest") |>
  arrange(desc(.data[[paste0("p_title_", levels(sims$model)[2])]])) |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("mean_wins"), ~ round(.x, 1)),
         across(starts_with("p_title"), ~ percent(.x, 0.1))) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Team", paste(c("Mean wins,", "Title %,"), rep(levels(sims$model), each = 2))[c(1, 2, 3, 4)]))
```

```{r title-plot}
title_odds |>
  group_by(team) |> mutate(ord = max(p_title)) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(team = reorder(team, ord), focus = team == FOCUS_TEAM) |>
  ggplot(aes(team, p_title, fill = model, alpha = focus)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1, `FALSE` = 0.55), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#006BB6", "#F58426")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Simulated championship probability (Knicks fully opaque)", x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL)
```

```{r anomaly-metrics}
anomaly <- title_odds |>
  group_by(model) |>
  mutate(rank = rank(-p_title, ties.method = "min")) |>
  summarise(
    p_knicks    = p_title[team == FOCUS_TEAM],
    rank_knicks = rank[team == FOCUS_TEAM],
    # chance that a typical season's champion has title odds at or below the Knicks'
    p_longshot  = sum(p_title[p_title <= p_title[team == FOCUS_TEAM]]),
    .groups = "drop")

anomaly |>
  transmute(Model = model,
            `P(Knicks win title)` = percent(p_knicks, 0.1),
            `About 1 in` = round(1 / p_knicks),
            `Rank among 30 teams` = rank_knicks,
            `P(champion is a team at least this unlikely)` = percent(p_longshot, 0.1)) |>
  kable()
```

The last column is the cleanest "anomaly" measure: in a typical
simulated season, how often does the champion turn out to be a team with
title odds no better than the Knicks'? A large number means a champion
like the Knicks is ordinary. A small number means it would be a genuine
surprise.

::: callout-note
## Interpreting "anomaly"

Ratings are estimated from the same 82 games that define the standings,
so the *average* simulated Knicks record sits near their actual record.
The informative quantity is the **spread** of seasons a team of that
quality could have had, and the resulting title probability. Neither
model captures playoff-specific effects (shortened rotations, star
usage, injuries, in-season roster changes). A team that was truly better
in the playoffs than its regular-season profile suggests will look
"lucky" here.
:::

### Finals matchups

Every simulation records the champion and the runner-up, so matchup
events come for free (the event "Team A and Team B make the Finals and
Team A wins" from the project description).

```{r finals-matchups}
finals <- sims |>
  filter(rounds_won >= 3) |>
  group_by(model, sim) |>
  summarise(champion = team[rounds_won == 4], runner_up = team[rounds_won == 3], .groups = "drop")

finals |>
  count(model, champion, runner_up, sort = TRUE) |>
  group_by(model) |> slice_head(n = 8) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(p = percent(n / N_SIMS, 0.1)) |>
  select(Model = model, Champion = champion, `Runner-up` = runner_up, `P(this exact result)` = p) |>
  kable()
```

When the Knicks win the title, whom do they beat?

```{r knicks-finals}
finals |>
  filter(champion == FOCUS_TEAM) |>
  count(model, runner_up) |>
  group_by(model) |> mutate(`Share of Knicks titles` = percent(n / sum(n), 0.1)) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 5) |> ungroup() |>
  select(Model = model, `Runner-up` = runner_up, Titles = n, `Share of Knicks titles`) |>
  kable()
```

## Seeds and championships

How likely is each **playoff seed** (1–8, after the play-in, pooled
across both conferences) to win a round, reach the Finals, and win the
title?

```{r seed-table}
seed_tbl <- sims |>
  filter(!is.na(playoff_seed)) |>
  group_by(model, playoff_seed) |>
  summarise(
    p_win_r1      = mean(rounds_won >= 1),
    p_conf_finals = mean(rounds_won >= 2),
    p_finals      = mean(rounds_won >= 3),
    p_title       = mean(rounds_won == 4),
    titles        = sum(rounds_won == 4),
    .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(share_of_all_titles = titles / N_SIMS)

seed_tbl |>
  transmute(Model = model, Seed = playoff_seed,
            `Win R1` = percent(p_win_r1, 0.1),
            `Reach conf finals` = percent(p_conf_finals, 0.1),
            `Reach Finals` = percent(p_finals, 0.1),
            `Win title (a given team with that seed)` = percent(p_title, 0.1),
            `Share of all titles` = percent(share_of_all_titles, 0.1)) |>
  kable()
```

## Reusable queries

Everything above can be regenerated from the saved `sims` table
(`readRDS("nba_sims_2026.rds")`).

```{r helpers}
# P(team wins title | team lands a given playoff seed), by model
title_given_seed <- function(team_name, seed) {
  sims |> filter(team == team_name, playoff_seed == seed) |>
    group_by(model) |> summarise(n = n(), p_title = mean(rounds_won == 4), .groups = "drop")
}
title_given_seed(FOCUS_TEAM, 1)

# Which teams win the most titles?
title_odds |> arrange(model, desc(titles)) |> group_by(model) |> slice_head(n = 5) |>
  select(model, team, titles, p_title) |> kable(digits = 4)
```

## Notes and limitations

- **Team strength constant within Model 1.** Model 1's ratings don't
  change during the season; Model 2's do, but only through recent
  scoring.
- **Offense/defense come from points per game, not per possession.** The
  schedule feed has final scores only, so fast- and slow-paced teams are
  not separated and opponent strength is not adjusted for. Adding
  possessions (from team box scores) or opponent-adjusted scores would
  sharpen Model 2.
- **Model 2 in the playoffs is frozen** at end-of-regular-season scores
  and not updated through the playoffs.
- **Model 2 simulation needs a points model.** Winners come from the
  Bradley-Terry probability and points are generated consistently with
  them; a team's *true* offense/defense inside the simulation come from
  the full-season points model, so these are in-sample estimates
  (uncertainty is included through the parameter draws).
- **Tuning constants** (`HALF_LIFE`, `PRIOR_GAMES`) were not optimized.
  They can be tuned by out-of-sample log-loss, as in the comparison
  above.
- **Seeding tiebreakers** are random rather than the official NBA rules,
  and home-court advantage is one league-wide constant.
- **Injuries, trades, and rest** are not modeled.
- `PARAM_UNCERTAINTY <- FALSE` reproduces point-estimate-only
  simulations, which are more concentrated (overconfident) than reality.
